newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM acts to defuse fuel surcharge dispute.
newsitem.headline: KLM acts to defuse fuel surcharge dispute.

text.p: KLM Cargo, the airfreight wing of KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, said it has agreed to improve communications with its Dutch shipper customers over controversial fuel surcharges.
Spokesman Peter Wellheuner said this had resulted from a meeting between the cargo division's management and the air freight shippers' council of leading Dutch transporters association EVO.
The meeting was arranged in the wake of a series of complaints by EVO about air cargo surcharges introduced by KLM and other airlines operating in the Dutch market.
EVO had claimed airlines which introduced cargo surcharges in response to high fuel prices had contravened the Treaty of Rome.
KLM said the talks had focused on the way its surcharge price rise had been introduced.

"We have agreed that both parties will communicate more in future. If it is necessary to introduce such a surcharge again, we have agreed to give more notice of any plans of this kind and to communicate our needs to the market better," Wellheuner said in a telephone interview.
He added: "We also made the point that KLM had been suffering from high fuel prices for quite some time before introducing an increased surcharge."
KLM Cargo added a fuel surcharge on shipments worldwide from November 1 this year.
The Dutch airline applied a worldwide increase of 20 guilder cents per kilo, or the equivalent in local currency.
